title: From Vieta to Chebyshev: A Unified Trigonometric Census of Polynomial Roots
summary: This article gives a trigonometric method for counting how many roots of a polynomial are real and how many are complex, without solving the equation. For a depressed polynomial $P(t) = t^d + c_{d-2}t^{d-2} + \cdots + c_1 t + c_0$ of degree~$d$ with $c_{d-2} < 0$ (the case $c_{d-2}\geq 0$ is discussed briefly in Section~\ref{sec:cgeq0} but not resolved), the substitution $t = u\cosθ$, $u = 2\sqrt{-c_{d-2}/d}$, matches $P$ against the Chebyshev identity $T_d(\cosθ) = \cos dθ$ and reduces the classification problem to a single trigonometric equation $f(θ) = \sum_{k=1}^{d-3}α_k\cos^k\!θ+ \cos…
